queries.text:
WITH RECURSIVE countdown AS (
  SELECT CAST(? AS SIGNED) AS n
  UNION ALL
  SELECT n - 1 FROM countdown WHERE n > 1
)
SELECT n FROM countdown
queries.name: Countdown

queries.text:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT title_id, count(*) AS view_count, CAST(rank() OVER (ORDER BY count(*) DESC) AS UNSIGNED) AS place
  FROM views GROUP BY title_id
)
SELECT t.id, t.name, ranked.view_count, ranked.place
FROM titles t JOIN ranked ON ranked.title_id = t.id
WHERE ranked.view_count >= CAST(? AS UNSIGNED) AND t.status = ?
ORDER BY ranked.place, t.id
queries.name: PopularTitles
comments: sqlc's MySQL engine cannot see a CTE from another CTE, nor type a parameter compared
with a CTE column, so one CTE and a cast on the parameter.

queries.text:
WITH picked AS (
  SELECT id, name FROM titles WHERE id IN (/*SLICE:ids*/?)
)
SELECT id, name FROM picked WHERE name <> ? ORDER BY id
queries.name: PickTitles
comments: A slice inside the CTE, then a scalar after it: the values stay in textual order.

queries.text: SELECT label, small, medium, big, ubig, precise, flag, bits, at_local, at_time, year_made, fixed, body, raw, kind FROM misc WHERE label = ? LIMIT 1
queries.name: GetMisc
comments: Every column type the type map knows, plus the string fallback (time, set).

queries.text:
INSERT INTO misc (label, small, medium, big, ubig, precise, flag, bits, at_local, at_time, year_made, fixed, body, raw, kind)
VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
queries.name: CreateMisc

queries.text: SELECT count(*) AS count FROM misc
queries.name: CountMisc

queries.text: DELETE FROM misc
queries.name: DeleteAllMisc

queries.text: SELECT id, name, status, price, rating, meta, poster, is_public, published_on, created_at FROM titles WHERE id = ?
queries.name: GetTitle
comments: One title by id.

queries.text:
SELECT id, name, price FROM titles
WHERE status = ? AND (price >= ? OR ? IS NULL)
ORDER BY id
queries.name: ListTitlesByStatus
comments: sqlc types a parameter from its first use, so the comparison has to come before IS NULL.

queries.text: SELECT id, name FROM titles WHERE id IN (/*SLICE:ids*/?) AND status = ?
queries.name: ListTitlesByIds
comments: Anonymous ? after the slice: sqlc numbers it 1 and the slice 2, but the values go in textual order.

queries.text: SELECT id FROM titles WHERE status = ? AND (id IN (/*SLICE:ids*/?) OR name IN (/*SLICE:names*/?))
queries.name: ListTitlesByIdsOrNames

queries.text: SELECT id FROM titles WHERE id IN (/*SLICE:ids*/?) OR id IN (/*SLICE:ids*/?) ORDER BY id
queries.name: ListTitlesByIdsTwice
comments: The same slice twice: sqlc emits two parameters and two markers.

queries.text:
INSERT INTO titles (name, status, price, meta, poster, is_public, published_on)
VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
queries.name: CreateTitle
comments: MySQL has no RETURNING; :execlastid returns the AUTO_INCREMENT id instead.

queries.text: UPDATE titles SET name = ? WHERE id = ?
queries.name: RenameTitle

queries.text: DELETE FROM titles WHERE id = ?
queries.name: DeleteTitle

queries.text: SELECT 'it\'s `tick` ${x} ? \n' AS literal, `price` FROM titles ORDER BY id LIMIT 1
queries.name: QuotedLiteral
comments: Backticks and ${} in SQL must survive the template literal: `a` ${b}
A '?' inside a string literal is not a parameter, nor after a backslash-escaped quote.

queries.text: SELECT id, name FROM titles ORDER BY id LIMIT ? OFFSET ?
queries.name: ListTitlesPaged

queries.text: SELECT count(*) AS count FROM titles
queries.name: CountTitles
comments: MySQL names an unaliased expression column by its text (`count(*)`), not the `count`
sqlc guesses, so expression columns need an alias here.

queries.text: SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM titles WHERE id = ?) AS title_exists
queries.name: TitleExists

queries.text:
UPDATE titles
SET name = COALESCE(?, name),
    status = COALESCE(?, status),
    price = COALESCE(?, price)
WHERE id = ?
queries.name: UpdateTitle
comments: Only the fields given change; sqlc.narg() makes each one optional.

queries.text:
INSERT INTO titles (id, name) VALUES (?, ?)
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE name = VALUES(name)
queries.name: UpsertTitle

queries.text: UPDATE titles SET status = 'published' WHERE id IN (/*SLICE:ids*/?)
queries.name: PublishTitles

queries.text:
SELECT id, name FROM titles
WHERE id NOT IN (/*SLICE:ids*/?) -- what about this ? here
  # or this ? one
  /* or this ? */
ORDER BY id
queries.name: ListTitlesNotIn
comments: Comments inside the statement are skipped by the placeholder scanner, '?' and all.

queries.text:
INSERT INTO views (title_id)
SELECT ? FROM DUAL WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM titles WHERE id = ?)
queries.name: RecordView
comments: The same parameter twice: sqlc emits two parameters with one name (the second untyped);
they become one argument, bound at both places.

queries.text:
WITH recent AS (
  SELECT title_id, CAST(max(viewed_at) AS DATETIME) AS last_viewed_at FROM views GROUP BY title_id
)
SELECT t.id, t.name, recent.last_viewed_at
FROM titles t JOIN recent ON recent.title_id = t.id
ORDER BY recent.last_viewed_at DESC
queries.name: RecentlyViewedTitles

queries.text:
SELECT t.id, count(v.title_id) AS views, CAST(max(v.viewed_at) AS DATETIME) AS last_viewed_at
FROM titles t
LEFT JOIN views v ON v.title_id = t.id
GROUP BY t.id
ORDER BY t.id
queries.name: TitleViewStats
comments: max() over an outer join is null for titles nobody viewed, and sqlc cannot type it
without the cast; it still reads the cast as NOT NULL.
@nullable last_viewed_at

queries.text:
SELECT t.id, v.viewed_at
FROM titles t LEFT JOIN views v ON v.title_id = t.id
WHERE v.viewed_at IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY v.viewed_at DESC, t.id
queries.name: ViewedTitles
comments: The WHERE rules out the LEFT JOIN's nulls, which sqlc cannot see.
@notnull viewed_at

queries.text: DELETE FROM views
queries.name: DeleteAllViews
